# agent-config

> Short Agent Skills for coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Pi): the agent asks once, then does reversible work and reports what it decided. FAILURES.md logs the failure each skill targets and how strong the record is.

Install all skills, not a subset: they hand off to each other by name, and `working-style` carries the always-on rule.

## Start here

- [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md): steps for an agent to install, verify, update and remove the skills
- [skills.json](skills.json): index of every skill with its description, stage, failure fixed and startup cost
- [FAILURES.md](FAILURES.md): per skill, the failure it targets and where that failure is recorded
- [evals/README.md](evals/README.md): behaviour tests in the `claude plugin eval` format, and how to run them

## Skills

<!-- skills-list:start (generated by scripts/build-index.mjs from skills/; do not edit) -->
- [brainstorm](skills/brainstorm/SKILL.md): Think a new project through with the user before anything is built: interview, research, write the design. Use for "brainstorm", "new project", or starting from scratch.
- [grilling](skills/grilling/SKILL.md): Stress-test a plan or decision in short rounds of pointed questions, each with a recommended answer. Use for "grill me", "poke holes in this", "challenge my plan".
- [research](skills/research/SKILL.md): Answer a defined question from primary sources, with dated citations. Use for "research X", "find out", docs or API facts, comparing options. Not for explaining this codebase.
- [prototype](skills/prototype/SKILL.md): Build a throwaway artifact to settle one uncertain design question. Use for "prototype", "spike", "mockup", "try a few versions", "what should this look like". Skip when behavior is settled.
- [writing-plans](skills/writing-plans/SKILL.md): Turn an approved design into a plan of small, testable tasks with exact files and checks. Use for "write a plan", "plan this out", or before multi-step work.
- [to-issues](skills/to-issues/SKILL.md): Break a design or plan into issues with dependencies and publish them to GitHub, Linear or Markdown. Use for "break this into issues", "create tickets", "make a backlog".
- [architecture-design](skills/architecture-design/SKILL.md): Settle module boundaries, interfaces and ownership before coding, or restructure code without changing behavior. Use for "design this", "refactor", "restructure", "how should we split X".
- [implement](skills/implement/SKILL.md): Carry an approved plan or issues to done, task by task, with tests and review. Use for "implement this", "build the plan", "work the issues", "start on ticket X".
- [working-style](skills/working-style/SKILL.md): Proceed, then present: do reversible work, report why. Ask only about product direction, or before irreversible or outward-facing steps: force-push, shared merge, deleting data, publishing, messaging people.
- [orchestrate](skills/orchestrate/SKILL.md): Coordinate implementer and reviewer agents on tickets in parallel worktrees. Use for "orchestrate", "run the factory", "work the backlog", "keep agents busy".
- [test-driven-development](skills/test-driven-development/SKILL.md): Build features and fix bugs test-first: a failing test, then the code that passes it. Use for TDD, "test-first", "write a failing test", "then make it pass", or regression tests.
- [systematic-debugging](skills/systematic-debugging/SKILL.md): Find the root cause of bugs, test failures, regressions, flaky or slow behavior before fixing. Use for "debug this", "diagnose", "why does X fail", or anything broken, throwing or slow.
- [frontend-design](skills/frontend-design/SKILL.md): Design and build web UI that does not look like a template or AI output. Use for building or restyling pages, components or dashboards, "make it look good", or deciding UX flows.
- [verification-before-completion](skills/verification-before-completion/SKILL.md): Gate any claim that work is done, fixed, passing or ready on fresh evidence. Use right before saying "done", "fixed" or "passing", handing work back, committing or opening a PR.
- [create-verification-skill](skills/create-verification-skill/SKILL.md): Write a verify-<app> skill so any agent can launch the app, drive a feature and capture proof. Use for "make a verification skill", or when agents claim done without running the app.
- [impact-review](skills/impact-review/SKILL.md): Review a diff or PR for spec and standards fit, and trace what it could break beyond the diff. Use for "review this", "code review", "what could this break", "blast radius", or review feedback.
- [ci-pr-lifecycle](skills/ci-pr-lifecycle/SKILL.md): Get a branch, PR and CI to done. Use for "is this ready", "CI status", "open a PR", "push and watch CI", "retry the failed job". Never merges unless asked.
- [explain-codebase](skills/explain-codebase/SKILL.md): Explain how existing code works and why it is shaped that way. Use for "how does X work", walkthroughs, "where should this live", "why is this here". Read-only.
- [wait-what](skills/wait-what/SKILL.md): Re-pitch your last message when it did not land. Use for "wait, what", "I don't get it", "explain that normally", "in plain English". One turn; no research.
- [handoff](skills/handoff/SKILL.md): Write a handoff brief so another agent can carry on, or resume work from one. Use for "hand off", "write up where we are", "pick up where we left off", "resume the last session".
- [reflect](skills/reflect/SKILL.md): Mine the current session for durable lessons and turn each into an edit to a skill or AGENTS.md. Use for "reflect", "what did we learn", "update the skills from this session", or a repeated mistake.
- [technical-documentation](skills/technical-documentation/SKILL.md): Write or revise docs checked against the code: READMEs, how-to guides, references, step-by-step guides for non-technical users. Use for "write a README", "document this".
- [unslop](skills/unslop/SKILL.md): Remove AI tells from prose, keeping facts and voice. Use on reports, docs, READMEs and PR text, or for "humanize", "tighten", "de-slop". Skip code, logs and quotes.
<!-- skills-list:end -->
